Savory

SAY-vuh-ree · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Savory is having a pleasant, salty or rich taste rather than a sweet one.

The catering table split the appetizers in two: delicate fruit tarts on one end, savory cheese-and-herb pastries on the other.

Worked Example

The food truck's menu board split neatly down the middle: sweet crepes on one side, savory crepes filled with ham and cheese on the other.

The ham-and-cheese crepes weren't dessert at all -- they were rich and salty rather than sugary, exactly what savory describes.

How Savory Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

umami

umami: a rich, savory taste sensation

appetizing

appetizing: having a pleasing taste that stimulates appetite

Antonyms

sweet

sweet: having the taste of sugar; not savory

sugary

sugary: tasting strongly of sugar

How Strong Is It? — plain → savory → rich

plain vs. savory

plain vs. savory: A plain dish has little flavor of its own, far less rich than something savory.

rich vs. savory

rich vs. savory: Something rich in flavor goes even further than savory, packed with deep, satisfying taste.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — savor-

root — savor-: taste, flavor (from Latin sapor, itself from sapere, 'to taste, to know' -- the Latin p softened to v on its way through French)

suffix — -y

suffix — -y: characterized by (English)

Put it together

Put it together: Savory is built from savor- ('taste, flavor,' from Latin sapor, itself from sapere, 'to taste' or 'to know' -- the Latin p softened to v on its way through French) + -y ('characterized by'). The same deep root gives us the rarer word sapient, describing someone wise -- to taste well and to know well were once the same idea.

Use the root in a new word: sapient

Use the root in a new word: sapient: The ancient text claimed that only a truly sapient ruler could tell friend from flatterer.

Root Check

Word Choice

Savory describes the salty, rich side of the flavor scale, as opposed to sweet -- unlike piquant, which describes a pleasant sharpness that can belong to either side.
